body.p: Claims 1-7, 9-17, and 19-20 are pending in the present application. Claims 1, 7, 9, 11, 17, and 19 are amended in this paper. Claims 8 and 18 are canceled in this paper. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not

necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications.

A telephonic interview regarding the instant matter was conducted on August 14, 2023, between Examiner Sanderson and Applicant's representative, Warren Conway, Reg. No. 81,846.Patentability under 35 U.S.C. § 103 was discussed. Applicant thanks the Examiner for his time and consideration in conducting the interview. During this interview, an agreement was reached that claims 1 and 11 as amended overcome the references of record.

The Examiner has objected to the drawings because of a minor informality consisting of reference sign "208" missing from FIG. 10 and reference sign "1005" missing from the description of FIG. 10. Paragraphs [0058] and [0061] have been amended to remove reference sign 208 and replace it with reference sign 1005. Applicant submits that this change has introduced no new matter. Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the objection.
Claim 9 is rejected pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 112 as allegedly indefinite for failing to
particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor regards as his invention. This rejection is traversed for the following reasons.
Without conceding the propriety of the rejection, and in the interests of advancing

prosecution, claims 9 and 19 have been amended to recite "the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear are housed within a blended wing body (BWB)." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this rejection of claim 9 under 35 U.S.C. § 112 be withdrawn.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that all rejections of claims pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 112 be removed.
Page/Messier

Claims 1-5, 7, 9-15, 17, 19, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over US Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0001999 to Page et. al. (hereinafter "Page") in view of US Patent Publication No. 1,847,491 to Messier (hereinafter "Messier"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Solely in the interest of expedited prosecution, and while not acquiescing to the Examiner's position, Applicant has amended claim 1 to now recite, (emphasis added):
A landing gear for an aircraft comprising:
at least a nose gear disposed longitudinally forward of a center of gravity of an aircraft by
a first distance and connected to a nose linkage configured to transfer movement
from the at least a nose gear to at least a main gear;
at least a main gear disposed longitudinally aft of the center of gravity of the aircraft by a
second distance and connected to a main linkage configured to transform
movement from the at least a main gear to the at least a nose gear; and
wherein the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear are mechanically linked using
a longitudinal member, wherein the longitudinal member comprises a tension
cable.

The Office does not assert that Page teaches, suggests, or motivates "at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear are mechanically linked using a longitudinal member, wherein the longitudinal member comprises a tension cable" Applicant respectfully submits none of what Page discloses, teaches, or suggests is any longitudinal member comprising a tension cable that is mechanically linking at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Page fails to disclose, teach, or suggest Applicant's particularly claimed system and limitations, as detailed above.
Messier fails to rectify the deficiencies of Page. The Office also does not assert that

Messier teaches, suggests, or motivates "the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear [...] mechanically linked using a longitudinal member, wherein the longitudinal member comprises a tension cable." The Office asserts that Messier discloses the mechanical linkage of "the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear," at FIG 4 of Messier, stating in part "a raising or lifting system with hydraulic control, constructed in such a manner that the lack of pressure in the pipe lines or cylinders, instantaneously causes the descent and locking of the Wheels in their lowered position." However, the above quoted language does not teach suggest or motivate "the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear [...] mechanically linked using a longitudinal member, wherein the longitudinal member comprises a tension cable" as disclosed in claim 1 as amended. Therefore, and for at least this reason, Applicant respectfully submits that Messier fails to disclose, teach, or suggest Applicant's particularly claimed system and limitations, as detailed above, and claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Page and Messier, alone and in combination.

Independent claim 11 recites limitations similar to independent claim 1 and overcomes these rejections for at least the same reasons as discussed above with reference to claim 1. Thus, Applicant submits that claim 11 is also patentably distinguishable over Page and Messier, alone and in combination.

Claims 2-7, 9, and 10 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. Claims 12-17, 19, and 20 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 11. As noted above, claims 1 and 11 are patentably distinguishable over Page and Messier, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 2-7, 9, 10, 12-17, 19 and 20 are patentably distinguishable over Page and Messier, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of these rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
Page/Messier/Sikorsky
Claims 8 and 18 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over
Page in view of Messier, in further view of US Patent Publication No. 2,630,989 to Sikorsky et. al. (hereinafter "Sikorsky"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
The rejection of claims 8 and 18 is moot because claims 8 and 18 have been cancelled. However, the subject matter of dependent claims 8 and 18 have been incorporated into independent claims 1 and 11.

Sikorsky does not cure the above-described deficiencies of Page and Messier. The Office asserts that Sikorsky discloses "the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear [...] mechanically linked using a longitudinal member, wherein the longitudinal member comprises a tension cable," at Column 2, Lines 9-14 of Sikorsky, stating in part "[[t]]he valve 34 is operated by a flexible control cable such as the Bowden wire 3% which is connected to the movable element 38 of the shock strut M on the landing gear 12 while the valve 32 is manually operated by a pilot control handle 40 Via a similar control cable 42." However, as agreed to in the above mentioned applicant initiated interview, the above quoted language does not teach suggest or motivate "the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear [...]mechanically linked using a longitudinal member, wherein the longitudinal member comprises a tension cable" as disclosed in claim 1 as amended. Therefore, and for at least this reason, Applicant respectfully submits that Sikorsky fails to disclose, teach, or suggest Applicant's particularly claimed system and limitations, as detailed above, and claims 1 and 11 as amended are patentably distinguishable over Page, Messier, and Sikorsky, alone and in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of these and all of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a

condition for allowance and respectfully solicit the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
